component: Tokens: --text-3 on --s2 and white text on the emerald accent
explanation: Found while migrating CaissaTrainer to the v0.1.0 tokens, measured from the token values. (1) --text-3 (#6f7371) on --s2 (#232424) is 3.24:1 (3.55:1 on --s1), below 4.5:1, so it cannot carry essential text such as placeholders, captions or counts. docs/DECISIONS.md D-007 already moved menu shortcut hints to --text-2 and left the token itself open; this is more evidence that the token is used for text people must read (the placeholder in the screenshot is an example). CaissaTrainer had to keep a rule: essential text is --text-2 or brighter. (2) White text on the emerald --accent (#10b981) is 2.54:1; --accent-ink (#04281d) on --accent is 6.24:1. Any text on an accent fill must use --accent-ink, never white; a migrated app inherited white-on-green from its old palette until a test caught it. The tokens.json usage note for --accent-ink says 'Text on accent fills' but no check or principle says white is wrong.

classification.rationale: Contrast of --text-3 (3.24:1 on --s2) and white on --accent (2.54:1) is not covered by a principle or check; PR-0001 already proposes CHK-023 for the first. Suggested: extend that check to cover text on accent fills and add the evidence to D-007's open question. The token-level decision stays with the owner.
